claims.statement: Determinate reality, as defined by Nonempty (Distinction α), entails the existence of two unequal values.
claims.boundary: Exact Lean definition of DeterminateReality and Distinction only.

claims.statement: If every pair of values is equal, determinate reality is impossible.
claims.boundary: NoDifference α := ∀ left right : α, left = right.

claims.statement: If every pair of values is equal, no InformationWitness sourced by a Distinction can exist.
claims.boundary: InformationWitness is the exact source-bound structure in UniversalOntology/Core.lean.

claims.statement: Am Anfang muss ein Unterschied gewesen sein, denn sonst wäre alles nichts.
claims.boundary: Beginning means ontological priority; nothing means absence of determinate difference.

claims.statement: The theorem proves a first physical instant or empirical cosmogenesis.
claims.boundary: Explicit negative boundary: no first-time, cosmogenesis, quantum-vacuum, or creation-from-nothing conclusion follows from the Lean theorems.

claims.statement: The physical universe instantiates the complete QIK-VRT Universal Ontology.
claims.boundary: Requires independent reference binding, operationalization, evidence, known-limit recovery, prediction and validation.

claims.statement: The formal theorem is identical to Leibniz's Principle of the Identity of Indiscernibles.
claims.boundary: Leibniz is a historical and conceptual reference; the QIK-VRT theorem is a distinct and weaker formal statement.

claims.statement: Zenodo publication by itself establishes scientific consensus or physical truth.
claims.boundary: Explicit boundary: Zenodo establishes persistence/identity/availability of deposited bytes, not scientific consensus or physical truth.

claims.statement: The public prose article traces a historical/conceptual line from the ontology of difference through Leibniz and later formal/technical developments to QIK-VRT.
claims.boundary: Explanatory historical synthesis; it is not a claim that every cited predecessor already contained QIK-VRT.

claims.statement: The Leibniz/QIK-VRT scientific PDF records a scholarly comparison and the dimensions in which QIK-VRT adds machine-checkable scope, provenance, successor semantics and effect evidence.
claims.boundary: Scholarly comparison artifact; the PDF itself does not establish empirical physical correspondence or scientific consensus.
